text:
Matt: Quick idea — run a crosswalk benchmark to ensure tokenizer+stopseq parity between model-A (quantized) and model-B (reference). Need strict apples-to-apples: same prompts, decode params, stop tokens, seed, and streaming vs non-streaming.

Lina: +1. Let's pin the tokenizer to a specific HF version and dump tokenization for every prompt so we can diff. Also prefer token-level stop checks, not substring match.

Raj: We should reuse the replay harness but force padding so sequence lengths are identical across models. Also capture KV cache metrics (hits/misses/inserts) per request.

Ana: Example harness command to start from (will tweak flags tomorrow):
```
./harness/replay \
  --model model-A \
  --prompt-file prompts.jsonl \
  --decode "temperature=0.0,top_k=1,stop=[\"\\n\",\"<END>\"]" \
  --tokenizer-lock "hf-tokenizer==0.13.4" \
  --dump-tokenization tokens-model-A.jsonl \
  --seed 42
```

Matt: Add runtime profiler flags when running long jobs:
```
RUNTIME_PROF=1 KERNEL_LOG=trace BATCH_HINT=max_latency_ms=20 ./run_load_test --workload crosswalk --runs 1000
```
This will emit kernel_choice events and per-token kernel timings.

Raj: Early smoke from a 1k paired run (summary):
- model-A (quantized) median latency: 180ms, p95: 420ms
- model-B (reference) median latency: 240ms, p95: 600ms
- Observed KV-cache "miss storm" around iteration ~540 on model-A (many requests showing repeated full-key recompute).

Lina: KV miss storm -> can cause fallback to slower kernel path (e.g., scalar decode). Check RT_TRACE logs for kernel switch events around that iteration. Also check whether batch sizes temporarily collapsed due to stragglers.

Ana: I pushed a small harness change that logs the following per-token metadata: `kernel_choice`, `kv_hit`, `batch_size_at_emit`, `decode_path`. Uploaded an artifact to CI: https://ci.internal/bench/2456789012/artifacts (will attach perf.json).

CI Bot: perf report uploaded: artifacts/2456789012/perf.json (SHA: abc123). Summary metrics included.

Matt: Another issue: decoding divergence at stop boundaries. model-B emits partial stop tokens which streaming flushes differently, causing off-by-one truncation compared to the dumped token sequences. We need to make stop enforcement token-level and deterministic across both runtimes.

Raj: Proposed test checklist for apples-to-apples: 
1) Tokenizer locked to exact version and same normalization flags.
2) Token-level stop checks (no post-decode string matching).
3) Deterministic sampling: seed pinned and fallback to greedy where sampling is nondeterministic.
4) Identical prompt trimming/whitespace handling before tokenization.
5) Collect per-token `kernel_choice` and `kv_hit` for later correlation.

Lina: Also include small-batch synthetic runs to exercise batching heuristics: `--batch-sim 1,4,8,16` and a `--kv-warmup` mode to prefill cache. Compare latency curves and batch-utilization.

Ana: I'll kick off a 5k paired run tomorrow morning. Gathering metrics: `median`, `p50/p95/p99`, `kv_hit_rate`, `kernel_switch_count`, `batch_utilization`, and tokenization diffs. Job id: `bench-crosswalk-2456789012`.

Matt: One more: add a regression alert if p95 increases >10% vs baseline model-B within the same job. Also flag any kernel_switch_count delta > 50% that correlates with latency spikes.

Lina: I'll wire a temp Grafana dashboard and a quick script to parse `perf.json` for those alerts. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Ana: scheduled the job and enabled `RUNTIME_PROF=1`. Will post artifacts link once done.

Matt: Thanks team. After the 5k run, let's meet and walk through: token diffs, KV hit/miss timelines, kernel choice correlation, and whether batching heuristic changes are required. :thumbsup:
